grants.programme: Direct Aid Program (DAP) — Serbia, North Macedonia & Montenegro
grants.summary: Australia's small-grants aid programme, managed by the Embassy in Belgrade, funds small-scale community and civil-society projects in Serbia, North Macedonia and Montenegro. It runs as an annual call — most recently open 15 September to 5 October 2025 — and the exact FY2026-27 opening/closing dates for the Belgrade round could not be confirmed today.
grants.eligibleActivity: DAP's own published priorities for Serbia/North Macedonia/Montenegro explicitly list 'promoting human rights, media freedom and good governance' alongside gender equality and youth priorities, so a documentation, reporting or public-education project on human rights, corruption or press-freedom issues sits under a named priority, not an inferred one. Funding is awarded to the project rather than to the applicant's profession, so an outlet would need to apply as, or in partnership with, a registered local NGO/CSO in Serbia, North Macedonia or Montenegro rather than as an individual freelancer.

amount.note: Up to AUD 20,000 per project, per the FY2025-26 Belgrade guidelines; the cap for the FY2026-27 round has not been independently reconfirmed.

grants.notes: Today's snapshot of the shared SmartyGrants portal is a landing page whose only followed live round was Cairo (Egypt), FY2026-27, closing 22 Sept 2026 — it did not confirm Belgrade-specific 2026-27 dates. WebSearch found the FY2025-26 Belgrade round ran 15 Sept - 5 Oct 2025, capped at AUD 20,000, with priorities 'human rights, media freedom and good governance', gender equality, youth-with-disabilities education/employment, and youth mental health. This is a corrected replacement for the previous seed entry, whose amount (EUR 10,000), currency and stated priorities (green transition) matched nothing found on the funder's own materials. Not confirmed on the funder's own page for the current round; check the SmartyGrants portal directly for the live Belgrade-specific deadline.

Requires a multi-country consortium; not something a single freelancer or newsroom can apply for alone. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: A Horizon Europe Cluster 2 call funding research into news consumption patterns and tools to help news media organisations and journalists adapt to digital transformation and reach new audiences. Up to three projects will be funded, each requiring a multi-country consortium including news media organisations.

amount.note: Estimated EU contribution per project for up to 3 projects.

grants.notes: Part of the Horizon Europe 2026-2027 work programme; exact call opening date not confirmed, so status is set to upcoming rather than open. Today's snapshot did not contain this call — details from web search. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: A free, 24/7 rapid-response service providing real-time technical assistance and cybersecurity advice to civil society groups, activists, media organisations, journalists, bloggers, and human rights defenders facing digital threats. The Helpline aims to respond to all requests within two hours and offers support in ten languages.

amount.note: Provides technical assistance, not a cash grant.

grants.notes: Today's accessnow.org snapshot covered the general 'Access Now Grants' grassroots-grantmaking page and a donor financial log, neither of which detailed the Helpline; details confirmed via web search of the funder's /help/ page. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.funder: ARIJ — Arab Reporters for Investigative Journalism
grants.summary: ARIJ awards grants of US$2,500 to Arab journalists to produce digital, audio, or televised investigative reports exposing environmental, legal, and financial corruption, separately covering filming and editing expenses. ARIJ's own site nav invites ongoing submission of investigation proposals alongside editorial mentoring and fact-checking support.

amount.note: US$2,500 per investigative report grant; ARIJ separately covers filming/video-editing expenses.

grants.notes: Today's snapshot of arij.net confirms a standing 'Submit an investigation' (قدم تحقيقاً) intake and references pausing responses over winter holidays, indicating an ongoing/rolling submission process, but did not capture ARIJ's dedicated grants page. The $2,500 amount and eligible-country list come from a search of ARIJ's own site (en.arij.net) rather than today's snapshot content. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.funder: Balkan Trust for Democracy (German Marshall Fund)
grants.programme: BTD Support for Western Balkans 6 — Media Freedom track
grants.summary: The Balkan Trust for Democracy funds civil society organisations registered in Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia and Serbia. One of its two current thematic tracks is strengthening media freedom (the other combats domestic and gender-based violence). Proposals are accepted on a rolling basis with no fixed deadline until the grantmaking budget is exhausted.
grants.notes: Today's snapshot of gmfus.org only captured generic GMF organisational pages (fellowships, donor FAQ) and never reached Balkan Trust for Democracy's own grant-call pages, so this entry is built from a search of GMF's own site. Only registered civil-society organisations in the six WB6 countries may apply — not individual freelancers. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.

grants.summary: A year-long, non-residential fellowship for activists, investigative journalists, filmmakers and lawyers to collaboratively investigate one pressing social-justice issue chosen around an annual theme. Reported support has included a fellow stipend, project funding, and a 'connect fund' for collaboration, plus training, mentorship and networking.

amount.note: Previously reported (secondary sources, prior cycle): fellow stipend up to US$64,900, project funding up to US$10,000, and a connect fund up to US$5,000.

grants.notes: Today's snapshot confirms the programme exists ('Fellowships for Activists, Investigative Journalists, Filmmakers and Lawyers to spend a year working on one pressing social justice challenge') and states verbatim: BERTHA FOUNDATION DOES NOT ACCEPT UNSOLICITED PROPOSALS — applications are only taken during announced windows. The most recent verified deadline (28 Jul 2025, for a fellowship year beginning Jan 2026) has passed; no 2026/2027 call was found open today. Programme appears to recur roughly annually. Not confirmed on the funder's own page for deadline/amount specifics.

grants.summary: Travel fellowships for journalists, journalism students and early-career science communicators to attend the World Conference of Science Journalists 2027 in London (6-9 September 2027), covering travel, visa costs, limited local transport, up to six nights' accommodation and conference registration. Selection weighs professional merit, motivation, and financial need.

amount.note: Covers travel, visa costs, limited local transport and up to six nights' accommodation, plus conference registration; no fixed cash amount stated.

grants.notes: GIJN's Grants & Fellowships aggregator page failed to fetch today (HTTP 403); found via web search referencing GIJN's listing and corroborated on the fellowship's own official registration site. Also independently surfaced via the GFMD aggregator; consolidated here since this version has a confirmed official application URL. Not confirmed on the funder's own page (GIJN's).

grants.summary: Astraea's International Fund gives flexible, core support to grassroots LGBTQI-led groups outside the US and Canada, across Africa, Asia/the Pacific, Eastern Europe/the former Soviet space, Latin America/the Caribbean and the Middle East. Grants back a group's own agenda rather than a single deliverable, and the foundation names media-making and storytelling among what it wants LGBTQI groups equipped to do.
grants.eligibleActivity: Astraea states its commitment is to 'equip [LGBTQI activists] with the tools to make their own media and control their own narratives,' so a media, storytelling or documentation project can be funded as core organisational work — but only for a grantee that is itself LGBTQI-led (Astraea explicitly does not fund groups without LGBTQI leadership), not for a general newsroom or freelancer applying on journalistic grounds alone. A freelance journalist would need to apply through, or as part of, a qualifying LGBTQI-led organisation.

amount.note: Applicant organisations must have an annual budget under USD 500,000; no specific per-grant ceiling was found stated.

grants.notes: Today's snapshot of astraeafoundation.org/grants/ was only a 145-word cookie-consent shell with no grant content (likely JS-rendered), so this entry relies entirely on WebSearch. The International Fund excludes the US and Canada and covers Africa, Asia/Pacific, Eastern Europe/former-Soviet countries, Latin America/Caribbean and the Middle East; whether Serbia specifically falls in Astraea's 'Eastern Europe' grouping was not confirmed, so geoScope is left as global rather than guessed. No specific 2026 deadline or grant-size ceiling was found; treat as an LOI-based rolling fund pending direct confirmation. Not confirmed on the funder's own page.
